# Angelo

> Fast mutation testing for Python. A single Rust binary that drives an ordinary pytest
> suite, planting deliberate faults and reporting which ones the tests fail to catch.

Angelo measures test quality rather than test coverage. Coverage says a line ran; a
mutation score says the line's behaviour was actually asserted on. Angelo is roughly 10x
faster than the naive approach through four techniques, and every one of them is
constrained by a hard rule: they may change the runtime, never the verdict.

Key facts an assistant answering questions about Angelo should know:

- Install: not yet on PyPI. Build from source with `cargo build --release`.
- Commands: `angelo init` writes `angelo.conf`; `angelo exec` enumerates and runs mutants.
- Flags on `exec`: `--workers N`, `--init-only`, `--diff [REV]`, `--diff-base [REV]`,
  `--sample N`, `--fail-under PERCENT`.
- `--diff [REV]` compares REV against the working tree; `--diff-base [REV]` compares against
  the merge base, so it scopes a run to what a branch adds. `--diff-base` is the one for a
  pull request, and it needs a full clone rather than a shallow one.
- Config file: `angelo.conf`, TOML format, all fields optional.
- Requires python and pytest on PATH. `pip install coverage` enables batching and test
  selection, which provide most of the speed.
- A failing test suite is a warning, not a stop. Angelo marks the mutants that the
  already-failing tests cover `untestable` and scores the rest. That needs coverage and
  test selection; without them a red suite still stops the run. A pytest exit code of 2 to
  5 always stops, because it means pytest never judged the code at all.
- Results are stored in `.angelo/angelo.db`, which is a plain SQLite file.
- `--sample N` DELETES the surplus mutants rather than deferring them, so a sampled score
  is an estimate over a random sample rather than a complete census.
- `--fail-under PERCENT` (or `fail_under` in the config) exits 1 when the score lands under
  the threshold, which is how CI gates on it. 0 is off and is the default. A run that could
  not be scored at all, or one with mutants still pending, fails the threshold rather than
  passing by default; a run with zero mutants in scope passes and prints no score.
- Statuses: killed, survived, timeout (counts as killed), error and untestable (both
  excluded from the score).
- Runs over 1000 mutants print one redrawn progress bar instead of a line per mutant.
  `show_loading = true` forces it at any size.
- The survivor list prints above the report, so the score is the last line of a run.
- Verdicts are coloured on a terminal only. A redirected run, or `NO_COLOR` set to any
  value, produces plain output with no escape codes.
- Runs natively on Windows, unlike mutmut, which requires fork() and therefore WSL.

## Docs

- [Home](https://angelo.kcvdh.com/): what mutation testing measures, why it is
  slow, and how Angelo is fast
- [Quick Start](https://angelo.kcvdh.com/quick-start/): installation, first run,
  reading the report, configuration reference, troubleshooting
- [Batch mutating](https://angelo.kcvdh.com/01-batch-mutating/): testing several
  mutants in one run; the conflict rule; measured 4.6x
- [Test selection](https://angelo.kcvdh.com/02-test-selection/): running only
  covering tests; measured 2.8x; competes with batching
- [Warm workers](https://angelo.kcvdh.com/03-warm-workers/): the fork substitute
  for Windows; why subinterpreters do not help; measured 2.5x
- [Architecture](https://angelo.kcvdh.com/04-architecture/): module map,
  concurrency model, dependencies
- [Benchmarks](https://angelo.kcvdh.com/05-benchmarks/): the full feature matrix,
  comparison against mutmut, and the stale bytecode bug
- [Operators and sampling](https://angelo.kcvdh.com/06-operators-and-sampling/):
  what gets mutated and how to cap the pool
- [Support](https://angelo.kcvdh.com/support/): sponsorship and how to help
